subject: Bundle granularity & minimum billing window — Atlas AI follow-up
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@atlas.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on bundle granularity / minimum window (SOW attached)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple follow-ups before we sign the SOW: we want to understand how Redwood's billing handles mixed short/long requests and whether KV cache reuse or conversation grouping reduces billable units across independent calls. Two concrete asks:

1) If a user does a mix of short prompt-response calls (under 100 tokens output) and occasional long-context analysis (10k token context), how do those get aggregated for billing? Are short calls grouped into a "bundle" during a retention window, or billed strictly per-call?

2) You mentioned a minimum billing window during the call. Is that a time-based retention (e.g., 5 minutes) or a token-quantum floor (e.g., 128 tokens)? Does dedicated capacity behave differently from hosted?

I attached the latest SOW for reference (Atlas_SOW_v2.pdf). Procurement also asked for a sample invoice calculation for a mixed workload so they can validate the numbers.

Appreciate a short written breakdown and if useful we can jump on a 20-min call.

—Samir
Head of Product
Atlas AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlas.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on bundle granularity / minimum window (SOW attached)

Samir —

Thanks — good, concise questions. Below is a short breakdown; I also attached a brief worked example and a Drive link with a step-by-step sample invoice. High level summary first:

- "Bundle granularity": by default for hosted customers we use a 2-minute activity window to group short requests from the same session/user into a single billable bundle. That means multiple calls from the same user within 2 minutes will be aggregated and charged against a single bundle quantum.

- "Billing quantum": hosted billing rounds up to 64-token quanta for generation and 256-token quanta for context storage charges. For Dedicated customers on committed capacity we can optionally set the quantum to 32 tokens (generation) and apply a lower context quantum depending on the commitment.

- "Minimums / retention window": the platform applies a 5-minute KV retention for short-session aggregation (this is different from the 2-minute bundle grouping; retention is used to allow fast re-use of KV across immediate retries or short follow-ups). Billing-wise we bill on the larger of (a) the bundle-aggregated tokens rounded to the billing quantum or (b) a per-call minimum of 192 tokens for hosted (this prevents large numbers of tiny calls from creating extreme operational overhead). For Dedicated customers we can waive the per-call minimum in favor of committed throughput usage.

Practical example (attached spreadsheet): if a user issues three short prompts within 90 seconds that each produce ~70 tokens of output, the 2-minute bundle groups them. Sum output token = 210 -> rounded up to 256 (64-token quantum) -> bill tracks 256 tokens. If during the same session they do a long-context job (10k context + 800 token output), context storage is metered separately per 1,024-token sliding window and rounded to 1,024 quanta.

On KV reuse: KV cache hits reduce compute but do not retroactively reduce already-billed bundles. They do reduce future billable generation because repeated prefixes are served from cache; we can also configure prefix deduplication for high-reuse flows which will reduce per-token charges.

Links / attachments: the Drive worksheet has two tabs — "mixed-workload-sample" and "dedicated-commit-options".

If you want, Vanessa can run the exact numbers against the Atlas expected traffic profile and produce a P&L-style comparison with and without a 20% discount tier.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlas.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@atlas.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on bundle granularity / minimum window (SOW attached)

Samir —

Looping in Ben from pricing to confirm how the Atlas discount would apply to mixed workloads. Quick notes from pricing perspective:

- Discounts apply to billable tokens after rounding. Example: if your rounded billable tokens for the month are 12,345, the discount percentage (e.g., 18%) applies to that final number.

- For committed Dedicated SKUs we can structure the contract so that the committed tokens are tallied weekly and unused committed tokens roll forward as credit (not a refund). That can help with bursty short-call patterns.

- On the SOW: we recommend a blended discount schedule tied to total effective billable tokens (after bundling and rounding) rather than separate discounts for "context" and "generation" to keep invoicing simple.

I've attached a quick sample calc (atlas-billing-sample.xlsx). Ben, can you confirm the numbers in tab "Sample A" reflect the 18% tier we discussed? Also, Samir — would you like the sample calc converted to your procurement template?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@atlas.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:34:00 -0800

Vanessa / Jordan —

This is super helpful, thank you. Two quick follow-ups before we finalize:

1) Can we get the sample calc in Atlas's PO template (yes please convert).
2) Procurement wants confirmation we get a small credit when KV reuse across canary rollouts prevents compute (they prefer an explicit KV-reuse credit rather than generic "efficiency" promises).

If those are straightforward, let's schedule a 20-min sync on Monday 11/22 to sign off. Otherwise I'll ask procurement for a short redline.

—Samir
